name: Office OAlerts
purpose: Captures the alert dialogs MS Office applications show users during risky or unsaved-work actions, such as attempting to close a document without saving.
key_fields: Event ID 300 - used by all Office applications for these alerts
Program name - which Office application generated the alert
Dialog message text - the specific alert text shown to the user
normal_baseline: Occasional Event ID 300 entries tied to routine unsaved-changes or file-format warnings during normal Office use, at a low, steady rate.
anomalies: A cluster of alerts around the time a document was closed or corrupted immediately following a suspected malicious macro execution
Alert text referencing a document type or feature (e.g. a compatibility or repair warning) inconsistent with the file the user claims to have been working on
Complete absence of any OAlerts entries on a system with heavy Office usage evidenced elsewhere in the timeline, suggesting the log was cleared
anti_forensic_notes: As a standard Windows Event Log, OAlerts.evtx can be cleared wholesale via wevtutil or the Event Viewer UI, which itself generates a Security log clear-event (Event ID 1102) - correlating the two logs can reveal deliberate clearing. Because every Office application shares the single Event ID 300, the dialog message text is required to distinguish alert types; the ID alone is not diagnostic.
interpretation: All Office alert types share the same generic Event ID 300, so filtering on ID alone returns every kind of Office warning - the program name and message fields must be read together to determine what specific action (unsaved close, format warning, etc.) triggered a given entry.
